newsitem.title: UK: Halifax sets 415p minimum shr auction price.
newsitem.headline: Halifax sets 415p minimum shr auction price.

text.p: Britain's Halifax Building Society, which has offered free shares to its customers as part of its flotation, said on Monday it would only sell those shares for its customers at 415p or more at auction.

The Halifax said it had offered its customers the chance to sell off their free shares seven days before the company is listed. The Halifax said institutions and London Stock Exchange firms had been invited to bid for the shares.

Many of Britain's building societies are taking advantage of new legislation to shed their mutual status and convert into publicly-listed banks, handing out free shares to millions of their customers in the process.

The Halifax, which is expected to give about nine million people shares, said it had offered to sell the stocks on behalf of its customers if they completed sale instruction forms and returned them by midday on May 26. The stock is expected to begin trading in London on June 2.

"Halifax Share Dealing Ltd will only sell the shares of any member whose sale instructions it receives on or before the day of listing if the price per free share that such members would receive would be at or above 415 pence," the building society said in a statement.
Financial institutions will bid for the shares in a bookbuilding process which will close on Friday May 30. The Halifax said it was starting roadshows on Monday to pitch the shares at institutions.
